This is game 51 in a series of 9×9 Go games. Each new game starts in a fresh session.

## Your goal

To become as strong at Go as you can: to keep improving, game after game, toward grandmaster-level play. The concrete target is to win consistently against the strongest opponent on the ladder, the 9d profile.

## What carries over

This session starts with no memory of the earlier ones: your conversation is not carried over. Your working directory does carry over: every file in it stays as you leave it. If CLAUDE.md exists there, it is loaded into your context at the start of every session; your other files are there to read with the file tools. What a later session knows of your earlier games is what you have left in these files.

Your working directory holds:
- CLAUDE.md (47,983 bytes)
- games.md (79,005 bytes)
- libs.py (813 bytes)

## This game

A new game. You play Black, so you move first.

Rules: Chinese area scoring, with 7 points of komi for White; a level score is a draw. Simple ko: an immediate recapture is refused, and the board marks the ko point when there is one. Suicide is not allowed. An invalid move is refused with the rule it broke, and the turn stays with you. The game ends after two passes in a row or a resignation; a game that reaches 243 moves is scored where it stands. After two passes the engine scores the position as it stands and decides itself which stones are dead.

## Opponents

Your opponent is KataGo playing in the style of a human of the rank you choose. The ladder, weakest to strongest: 20k, 18k, 16k, 14k, 12k, 10k, 8k, 6k, 4k, 2k, 1d, 3d, 5d, 7d, 9d. You choose the rank with `choose_opponent(rank)` before the first move; it holds for the whole game, and you choose again in the next game.

## Tools

- Go: `choose_opponent(rank)`, `board()`, `play(move)` with a point or `pass`, and `resign()`.
- Files: your Read, Write, Edit, Glob and Grep tools, for any file in your working directory.

You also have a shell, and you may write and run code in it; Python is available as `python3`. Use it only to inspect the current position and keep records — for example, to count stones or liberties, or check whether a move is legal. Do not build or use a Go engine, run Monte Carlo, search over sequences of future moves, or write a program that chooses, ranks or recommends moves.

## How this session ends

Play until the game is over. The final result comes back from your last Go call, followed by a closing note. Before you end the session after a game, write down in your working directory whatever will help the next session play better. The session ends when you end your turn.

# Usage: python3 libs.py <<< "board rows 9..1 as 9 lines of X/O/." ; prints groups and liberties
import sys
cols="ABCDEFGHJ"
rows=[l.split() for l in sys.stdin.read().strip().splitlines()]
rows=[r[1:10] if len(r)>9 else r for r in rows]
B={}
for i,r in enumerate(rows):
    for j,c in enumerate(r): B[(j,9-i)]=c
def nb(p):
    x,y=p
    for q in((x+1,y),(x-1,y),(x,y+1),(x,y-1)):
        if q in B: yield q
seen=set()
for p in B:
    if B[p] in"XO" and p not in seen:
        g=[p];libs=set();k=0;seen.add(p)
        while k<len(g):
            for q in nb(g[k]):
                if B[q]=='.':libs.add(q)
                elif B[q]==B[p] and q not in seen: seen.add(q);g.append(q)
            k+=1
        n=lambda s:",".join(sorted(cols[a]+str(b) for a,b in s))
        print(B[p],n(g),"libs:",len(libs),n(libs))
- Good: libs.py caught a 2-lib 9-stone group (C3 save). Capture F1 with ko worked but
  W's ko threat H8 was real: when I start a ko, list my own cut points first (H8).
- Invasion C8 late was free but W lived: W filled its own A4 eye but still had A6/B5
  as two shared eyes between its left group and main chain.

## Game 48 — White vs 12k — LOST (resigned move 34)
Moves: B G7, W C4, B G3, W E5, B C6 (approach above C4), W D7?, B D4 (wedge between
C4/E5), W D3, B C5, W D5 (atari), B E4, W E3 (atari), B F4 (connects toward G3), W C3
(C4 had 2 libs), B C7, W D6, B F6, W E7, B D8, W E8, B C8, W F5, B G5, W F3 (sente),
B G4, W F7, B G8, W F8, B B4, W E9, B G2, W G9, B H8 -> resigned.
Final: my 10-stone centre group D5-F8 had libs D9/E6/F9, eye points F9 (G9 weak) and
E6 (dies to black G6). Even if it had lived: centre ~14 + bottom ~18 = 32 < 38.
Takeaways:
- Opening C4 + E5 + D7 = three HIGH stones, only one with a base. Black C6, D4, F6,
  D8/C8, G5 sealed a white centre group with black on the left (C5-C8), right (F6/G-col)
  and below (D4-G4 chain linked to G3). Lesson 000 / Y1 again: sandwiched centre group.
- After B C6 (with G7, G3 already black), the 3rd move should be LOW: E3 (link C4,
  pincer G3, make rows 1-3 mine) or C7/D7 only if C4's bottom is already safe.
- B D4 wedge between C4 and E5: my D5/E3 ataris drove black's chain D4-E4-F4 to link
  with G3 and cut my stones in two. Consider E4 (keep E5 linked to the bottom) instead.
- Black tenukied (B4, G2) because my group was already dead: when the opponent
  ignores a group of mine that I think is fighting, count its eyes — it's probably dead.

## Game 49 — Black vs 12k — LOST (resigned move 41, ~31 vs ~50)
Moves: B C4, W F5, B G3, W E3 (wedge between my two bottom stones), B E4 (cap, cut E3
from F5), W F4, B F3, W D4 (E4 now in ATARI), B E5, W D5 (atari again), B E6, W D6,
B F6, W C3 (C4 at 2 libs), B G5 (atari F4-F5), W E7, B G4 (captured 2), W F7, B G7,
W G8, B H8, W H7 (cut, G7 atari), B G6, W F8, B H6, W E2, B F2, W F1, B G1, W E1,
B C5, W C6, B B6, W B7, B B5, W B3 (left group now 4 stones, libs A5/A6/B4, 1 eye max),
B C7?, W C8 (C7 in atari), B D2, W D3 -> resigned.
Takeaways:
- Same W F5 opening as G47 (C4 + G3 -> W E3 wedge). My E4 cap was answered by W F4
  and W D4, and E4 was in atari twice: I ended up running a 1-stone-wide line up the
  E column (E4-E5-E6) while W built D4-D5-D6 beside it. Capturing F4-F5 (2 stones) felt
  good but W got the whole left side (D column wall + C3 + C6) and the top (E7-G8).
  Area was ~33 for me at move 30 = loss already.
- vs W E3 wedge between C4 and G3: try D3 (attach from the side of my WEAKER stone C4,
  keeping the corner) or F3 (block from G3's side) and let E3 live small. The cap E4
  put a 3-lib stone between three W stones — it got ataried at once.
- vs W F5 as the 2nd move: G3 makes E3 the obvious wedge. Next time try C4 then a
  stone on the open LEFT/TOP side (C6/D7 area is too close...) — or E3 myself (low,
  under F5, connects toward C4, rows 1-3) then claim a second side.
- C5/B6/B5 rescue of C4 only made a bigger dead group (eye space A4-A6 + B4 next to W
  B3 = one eye). When the left corner has W C3 inside and W walls at C6/D-col, let C4 go.

## Game 50 — White vs 14k — WON W+2 (38 area + 7 vs 43)
Moves: B E5, W C4, B G7, W G3, B E3 (wedge), W D3, B C7, W F3 (attach on wedge),
B D4, W E2 (atari, forces E4), B E4, W C3 (D3 had 2 libs), B G5, W C5, B C6, W H4,
B H5, W G4 (solid, H4 cut point), B F4, W B6 (hane), B B7, W B5, B A6, W A5, B A7,
W D5, B D6, W J5 (hane), B J6, W J4, B H6. Boundary closed at move 32: my area =
A-C rows 1-5 + B6 + D1-D3 + D5 + E1-E2 + F-J rows 1-3 + G4/H4/J4/J5 = 38 exactly.
Then a free invasion E8/D8/F8/F7 in black's top died (eye space only D9-F9 row; black
G9/C9 kill it) - cost nothing under area scoring. F2 (solid), pass, pass.
Takeaways:
- vs tengen + G7: C4, G3 (both low on the open bottom) worked again (like G38). vs the
  E3 wedge: D3 (next to C4), then F3 attach, E2 atari (forces E4) then C3 solid.
- Every one of my stones was solid/attached; boundary moves in order: C5, H4, G4, B6/B5,
  A5, D5, J5/J4. 38 is a THIN win: one lost edge point = draw. Count at move ~20.
- Late invasion: needs room for 2 eyes on the edge; a 3-wide row 9 under black row-7
  stones isn't enough. Fine to try (free), but answer anything black plays in my area.

I won game 51 as Black against the 12k opponent, **B+8** (48 points of area against White's 33 + 7 komi).

- **Opening (C4, G3, E5):** White played F6, C7 and G5, so the board split along row 5. Around move 14 my count was about 39 to White's 49, so I was losing if I just played safe.
- **Turning point (E6):** White's wall had a one-point gap between D6 and F6, and all my groups were strong, so I cut there. Then D7 (atari), E7, D8, C8, E9 and D9 pushed a column of my stones up to the top edge, which gained about 9 points.
- **Finish:** I took the small edge points (A5/A4, C9, J4). Before passing I connected my top group to the bottom with E4, because its only liberties were D4, E4 and F4. White never invaded my empty bottom rows, and both sides passed.
